Three Rivers Messages Handbook

For front desk, Billing, providers and admins

How Messages works, from a patient's first message to Done.

Messages brings the practice's email, texts, calls, voicemails and faxes into the dashboard, grouped by patient. This handbook covers what each person sees, how to reply, match, hand off and finish, and the settings admins look after.

Chapter 01 of 14 · Start here

Messages at a glance

What feeds Messages, who sees what, and what never leaves Gmail or Spruce.

What Messages is

Messages is a page in the dashboard, in the left sidebar with the inbox icon. It shows the practice's correspondence in one place:

  • email in the practice Gmail mailboxes an admin has connected;
  • texts, calls, missed calls, voicemails and faxes on the Spruce lines an admin has turned on.

Messages groups everything by patient. When a conversation belongs to a Healthie patient, it shows under that patient, so one row holds their email and their texts together. Conversations that don't belong to a patient yet show on their own.

Gmail and Spruce stay as they are

Messages reads from Gmail and Spruce and sends through them; it doesn't replace either one.

  • Replies you send from Messages go out through the same mailbox or Spruce line, and they show in Gmail or Spruce too.
  • Done, Handled by, internal notes and who has read what live only in Messages. Marking a patient done doesn't archive anything in Gmail or change anything in Spruce.
  • Messages keeps only the sender, subject and a short preview for the list. The full text is read fresh from Gmail and Spruce each time you open a patient.

Who sees what

What you see depends on your role. An admin sets each person up in Settings › Messages access.

Sees Can also
Admin Every patient, and conversations not linked to anyone Everything, including the settings
Front desk Every patient, email included, and Needs matching Choose who handles a patient, link conversations to patients
Billing Only patients handed to Billing, with their email Hand a patient back to front desk
Provider Only patients handed to them, without email unless an admin adds it Hand a patient back to front desk

Front desk sees every patient and decides who handles each one. Billing and providers see a patient only after front desk hands it to them. Billing and providers has more on their side of it.

Getting in

Admins can always open Messages. Everyone else needs three things: one role on their dashboard account (staff or provider), the Messages switch turned on for staff, and their own setup in Settings › Messages access. If one is missing, the page says which:

  • Messages is not open to staff yet. The switch is off. Providers see this too.
  • An admin needs to set up your Messages access.
  • An admin needs to choose your team in Messages access.
  • Your account needs exactly one of the staff and provider groups.

With Demo Mode on, Messages hides itself, because it holds real patient correspondence.

Keeping it private

  • Internal notes are for the team. Patients never see them.
  • The dashboard signs you out after 30 minutes without activity, after a one-minute Still there? warning. Anything you haven't sent is lost, so send or copy it first.
  • If your access changes while you're working (an admin changes your setup, or a patient is handed to someone else), the page lets go of what you can no longer see and starts over.

Chapter 02 of 14 · Start here

The list

Patient rows and loose conversations, the filters, the chips, unread and search.

Two kinds of row

  • A patient row stands for everything linked to one Healthie patient: their email threads, their Spruce conversations, or both. When they have more than one conversation, a small number after the name says how many.
  • A conversation row is a conversation not linked to anyone yet: a new sender, a pharmacy, a vendor, a fax. This handbook calls these loose conversations.

A conversation linked to a patient never shows as its own row. You find it inside the patient.

What a row shows

  • The name. For a patient this comes from Healthie. For a loose conversation it's the sender, or Unknown number for a text from a number with no name.
  • The time of the latest activity: the time today, the date this year (Oct 21), or the full date for older ones.
  • A preview of the newest conversation. You: in front means the practice wrote last.
  • Chips:
  • the kind: Email, Text, Fax, Call, Missed call or Voicemail. Missed calls and voicemails are orange, because someone needs a call back.
  • Waiting 25m, Waiting 3h 59m and so on: how long someone has been waiting on the practice. See Done, waiting and unread.
  • Done: nothing is open.
  • Chart save to check: a file saved to the chart needs a look (see Save to chart).
  • Choose who handles: the patient's conversations were assigned to different people before, and someone should pick one owner.
  • @ Tagged: someone tagged you on this patient in a note. Hover over it to see who and when (see Tagging a teammate).
  • Initials in a circle: the person handling this patient, when it's someone by name.
  • On a loose conversation, a match chip: Which patient? or No patient in amber, Not a patient in gray, and Shared contact when a link was undone because the sender reaches more than one patient.

A blue dot and bold text mean unread for you. Unread is per person: your reading doesn't clear the dot for anyone else.

Tabs and filters

Inbox holds everything open. Front desk and admins also have Needs matching, with a count of conversations waiting for a patient (see Needs matching).

The chips narrow the Inbox:

  • All
  • Waiting: someone is waiting on the practice.
  • Mine: patients handled by you by name, and loose conversations assigned to you. Billing holds patients as a team, so Mine stays empty for Billing staff.
  • Tagged: patients you're tagged on. It shows only once someone has tagged you. For front desk it lists tagged patients even after they're done.
  • Email, Texts, Voicemail (missed calls included), Fax: by channel. A chip with nothing in it hides itself.
  • Done: patients and conversations with nothing open. It pages back with Load older.

Each chip except Done shows a count. A + after a count means there are more than the page could count.

The list refreshes itself every 30 seconds. On the Inbox, the round arrow refreshes it now. When there are more rows, Load more sits at the bottom.

Search

The search box finds rows by the patient's name or email as Healthie has them, and by sender and subject. Names need at least three letters. It doesn't search message text.

If many patients share the name, the list says Many patients match that name. Keep typing to narrow it. If Healthie can't be reached, it says Name search isn't working right now. Sender and subject still are.

Chapter 03 of 14 · Working a patient

A patient's timeline

Everything with one patient in one place: email, texts, calls, voicemails, notes and files.

The patient card

Open a patient row and their timeline fills the right side, starting at the newest message. The patient card stays at the top while you scroll, so you always see who this is:

  • name, with Discharged for an inactive patient;
  • Born, phone and email. On a narrow window this line is cut short; point at it to see all of it.

Under the name is a band with Group and Next visit (date, type and provider, or None booked). For front desk and admins it starts with Handled by (see Handled by and hand-offs).

On the right are Details, Open chart, Done and, for Billing and providers, Hand back. Details opens more from Healthie: address, any balance due, insurance and eligibility, and the latest appointments. Providers don't get it. Open chart opens their chart in Healthie in a new tab.

Call is in the reply bar at the bottom, next to Text and Internal note, so it's always in reach (see Calling a patient).

One timeline for every channel

Everything with the patient sits in one list, oldest at the top, newest at the bottom:

  • email messages;
  • texts, drawn as chat bubbles, the patient's on the left and the practice's on the right;
  • calls, missed calls and voicemails;
  • internal notes, labeled Staff only;
  • hand-off and hand-back notes, in violet.

A day line (Today, Yesterday, or the date) marks each new day. Items from the same conversation sit together under a source line, such as Email · Question about my refill or Spruce · (857) 555-0101, with a Waiting or Done chip.

In an email thread, the newest message is open and older ones are one line each. Click one to read it. A message sent from Messages says sent from the hub by and the name of whoever sent it.

Calls and voicemails

A call shows as Incoming call with its length, Outgoing call, Missed call or Voicemail. Missed calls and voicemails are orange: someone needs a call back. A voicemail shows Spruce's transcript in quotes, or Transcript in progress. or No speech in this voicemail. The recording is attached and plays in the preview.

An answered call is a record of a conversation that already happened. It never makes anyone wait.

Calling a patient

Call, in the reply bar at the bottom of the patient, calls the patient from your own phone, and they see the practice number, not yours. Your phone is the mobile on your entry on the People page, the person your dashboard login is linked to.

  1. Press Call. Call this patient? says what happens next. Press Set up call.
  2. Messages shows Dial now from your phone and a number to dial.
  3. From your phone, the one ending in the four digits shown, dial that number straight away. Spruce connects you to the patient.

It always calls the patient's number in Healthie; you can't type a different one. If nothing connects, close the box and set the call up again. Between 9pm and 8am the box warns that a call can wake people up.

If the call can't be set up, the box says why:

  • Your login is not linked to a person yet. An admin links your login to you on the Users page.
  • Your mobile is not on the People page yet. An admin adds it to your entry on People.
  • Your mobile is also on someone else on the People page. Each person needs their own mobile; an admin fixes it on People.
  • You are marked inactive on the People page, or your login is linked to two people. An admin fixes it on People or Users.
  • Calls are not set up yet. An admin chooses the line calls go out from in Settings › Inboxes.
  • Healthie has no phone number for this patient. Add one in Healthie first.
  • Spruce did not set up the call. Nothing rang. Try again, or call from Spruce.
  • Spruce did not confirm the call in time. Set it up again, and dial only the new number it gives you.

If you haven't dialed within two minutes, the box suggests setting the call up again.

Files

Attachments show as tiles with the file name, and the size for email attachments or the kind of file for Spruce ones. PDFs, images and audio open in a preview with a Download button; other files download straight away. Each time you open a file, Messages makes a short-lived copy for you, and that link stops working after a minute. Open the file again if you need it later.

Staff can save a file to the patient's chart with the button beside the tile. Save to chart covers it.

Faxes don't appear in a patient's timeline yet. They stay in the Inbox as their own rows (see Needs matching).

Long histories

The timeline loads a patient's five most recent conversations. Load 2 older conversations (or however many there are) fetches the next ones.

Banners above the timeline tell you when something is off:

  • One conversation has new activity since this opened. Press Refresh to see it.
  • A conversation that couldn't be read says why: it's no longer in Gmail or Spruce, its mailbox needs reconnecting in Settings › Inboxes, or it could not be loaded right now. It ends Done leaves it open.
  • Email about this patient stays with front desk and billing. You don't have email access, so their email isn't shown.

Chapter 04 of 14 · Working a patient

Replying and notes

Email replies, texts, quiet hours, internal notes, and what happens to a draft.

Where your reply goes

You reply in one conversation at a time. Messages picks the conversation the patient last wrote in. When the patient has more than one, Reply in at the bottom lets you choose: an email thread by its subject, a Spruce conversation by its number, or New email… to start a new thread (see New email). If you change Reply in with something typed, Messages asks before throwing it away.

A reply always goes out the way the conversation came in. An email reply goes from the conversation's own mailbox, and a text goes from the Spruce line the patient used.

Texting

Press Text. The box shows who it goes to and a character count out of 1,600. The footer says which line it Sends from.

  • Send sends it now. Send and mark done sends it and closes that conversation.
  • After sending, a card under the timeline shows Sending…, then Sent to Spruce. It will appear above in a moment. "Sent" means Spruce accepted it. Spruce doesn't report delivery.
  • Fax lines can't be answered here: the page says Faxes are answered in Spruce.

Quiet hours

From 9pm to 8am Eastern, a text can wake someone up. During those hours the text box shows It's quiet hours (9pm to 8am). Texts now can wake people up. and two buttons:

  • Send at 8:00 AM has Spruce send it at 8am. The card says Spruce will send this at 8:00 AM. You can cancel it in Spruce before then.
  • Send now sends it straight away.

The 8am time is shown in your computer's time zone. Send and mark done isn't offered during quiet hours, so mark the patient done separately.

Replying by email

Choose an email conversation under Reply in. The strip offers Reply, Reply all (when others were on the email), Forward and Internal note.

  • To and Cc hold addresses as chips. Type an address and press Enter; Backspace removes the last one. A bad address turns red.
  • The footer says which mailbox it Sends from. You can't change it.
  • Forward sends the newest message on with its attachments, and you can add a note above it. You can't attach new files from Messages. Very large attachments (over 20 MB together) have to be forwarded from Gmail.
  • Send, or Send and mark done to close the conversation once Gmail accepts the email.

The reply shows as a card under the thread until Gmail syncs it into the timeline: Sent. It will appear above once Gmail syncs.

When a send isn't confirmed

Sometimes Gmail or Spruce takes the message but doesn't answer in time. The card then says Not confirmed, for example Gmail hasn't confirmed this reply. It will appear above within a few minutes if it went out.

Don't send it again straight away. Wait a few minutes and look: at the timeline, the mailbox's Sent folder, or the conversation in Spruce. Messages never retries a send on its own, so nothing goes out twice unless you send it twice. Failed. Nothing was sent. means it definitely didn't go, and you can send again.

Internal notes

Internal note writes a note for the team on this conversation. It's never sent, and patients never see it.

Anyone who can open the conversation sees its notes, including a provider it's handed to. Notes stay in Messages; they don't appear in Gmail or Spruce. Press Save note.

Tagging a teammate

Front desk and admins can tag someone in an internal note, to ask them to look at a patient. Tagging works on a conversation linked to a patient, in the patient's timeline or in the conversation on its own.

  1. Press Internal note and start writing.
  2. Type @ and the start of a name. A list of people opens under the box, providers first. Pick someone with the arrow keys and Enter, or click them. Escape closes the list.
  3. Their name goes into the note as @Name, and a chip under the box says Tagging: and their name. Keep writing, then press Save note.

The chip also says if the person:

  • no Slack, sees it in Messages only: no Slack message can reach them, so they find out when they next open Messages.
  • can't see email, sees your note: on an email conversation, someone without email access sees your note but never the email.

You can tag up to five people in one note, but not yourself. To take someone off before saving, press the × on their chip, which also takes their @Name out of the text, or delete their @Name yourself.

When the note is saved, the page says Note saved. Tagged and the names, with a line for anyone the Slack message didn't reach. In the note, each tagged name is highlighted and Tagged: lists who.

Each person you tag:

  • gets a Slack message, if Slack can reach them, saying who tagged them, with a link to the patient. It never names the patient or repeats your note.
  • sees the patient on their list with a Tagged chip and your note on top, until they press Clear. They can read, reply, write notes and call. The rest stays with whoever handles the patient (see Billing and providers).

A tag doesn't change who handles the patient; to hand the patient over, use Handled by (see Handing off). Front desk and admins see who's tagged on a patient in the Handled by band (see Who handles a patient). Tagging someone again moves their tag to the newer note. If the conversation is later linked to another patient, the tag stops counting.

While Messages isn't open to staff, a tag on anyone but an admin is saved but does nothing until it's turned on, and no Slack message goes out.

Drafts

A reply you're writing lives only on the page, never in your browser's storage.

  • Messages asks Discard your draft? before you pick another row, go back to the list, mark the patient done, change Reply in, or go to another page from the sidebar. Keep editing keeps it.
  • Reloading or closing the tab gets your browser's own warning about leaving the page.
  • It's lost without asking if you're signed out after 30 minutes idle, or your access changes while you're writing. That's on purpose: nothing stays on screen after a sign-out.

The trash icon, Discard draft, throws the draft away without asking.

Chapter 05 of 14 · Working a patient

New email

Starting a new email thread with a patient, and what to do when Gmail doesn't confirm it.

Starting a new thread

To email a patient about something new, open the patient and choose New email… under Reply in. A new email starts its own thread and is filed under this patient straight away. Automatic matching never moves it.

  • From: a connected practice mailbox. If there are several, pick one.
  • To: only addresses this patient is known by: their email in Healthie, and any outside address that has written in on one of their email conversations. You can't type a new address here.
  • Subject: one line.

Press Send. The page says Email sent, or Email sent. It shows here once it is filed under the patient.

New email is for people with email access: admins, front desk, Billing, and providers an admin has given email. It only works for a patient who already has a conversation in Messages.

When it can't send

Sending stays off, with the reason, when:

  • the chosen mailbox is no longer connected (choose another, or ask an admin to reconnect it);
  • no mailbox is connected at all;
  • the address is no longer known for this patient;
  • This patient has no email address on file.

When Gmail doesn't confirm it

If Gmail doesn't answer in time, the draft locks: We couldn’t confirm Gmail sent this. If it went, it shows here after the next sync. This draft can’t be sent again; discard it to write a new one.

Under the timeline, a reminder says We couldn’t confirm a new email to the address went. Messages keeps checking for a day. After that it says the email is no longer checked automatically. Look in Gmail before writing again.

Look in the mailbox's Sent folder in Gmail. If it went, it will show up on the patient. If it didn't, discard the draft and write it again. I’ve checked, dismiss clears the reminder; it doesn't change anything in Gmail.

Chapter 06 of 14 · Working a patient

Done, waiting and unread

When a patient counts as waiting, what Done closes, and what brings a patient back.

Waiting

A conversation is waiting when someone reached out and the practice hasn't answered yet. The Waiting chip on a row counts from when the oldest unanswered message arrived.

These start a wait:

  • an email from outside the practice;
  • a text, missed call, voicemail or fax from the patient.

These answer it:

  • an email reply to someone who wrote in, whether sent from Messages or straight from Gmail;
  • a text you send the patient from Messages;
  • a text someone types in the Spruce app;
  • a fax sent from Spruce;
  • Done.

If the patient writes again while your reply is being sent, the conversation stays waiting. Answer the new message, or mark it done.

These don't answer it:

  • Spruce's automatic reply ("Thank you for your message…");
  • the practice's automated texts, like booking links and reminders, and bulk texts;
  • a text set for 8:00 AM, until Spruce sends it. If someone cancels it in Spruce, it never counts;
  • an internal note, a phone call you made, or forwarding an email to a colleague.

These still show in the timeline. An automatic reply never takes the place of what the patient wrote in the list. If you called the patient back, mark them done.

Done

Done sits at the top of the patient. It closes every conversation of theirs that you have access to, including older ones not loaded on screen, as long as nothing new arrived in them. Then it returns you to the list with Marked done.

Done won't close a conversation that changed after you opened the patient. When that happens, the message says what's still open and why, for example 1 closed. 1 still open: new messages arrived. Have a look, then mark done again. Other reasons:

  • a new conversation was added
  • moved to another patient
  • the contact reaches more than one patient
  • couldn't be loaded

Read what came in, then press Done again.

Done doesn't change who handles the patient, and it doesn't touch Gmail or Spruce.

What brings a patient back

A done patient comes back to the Inbox when:

  • the patient (or anyone outside) writes or texts again, or leaves a missed call or voicemail;
  • for front desk, Billing or a provider hands them back;
  • for Billing or a provider, front desk hands them over;
  • for front desk and admins, a file saved to the chart needs checking.

Your own replies never reopen a patient. There's no Reopen button on a patient; something new happening reopens it.

Unread

Opening a patient marks what you read as read, for you only. A patient timeline has no way to mark it unread again.

A loose conversation (not linked to a patient) works a little differently. At the top it has its own Done and Reopen, Mark unread, and an Assigned to menu for front desk to give it to someone.

The Done list

The Done chip lists patients and conversations with nothing open, newest first. Load older goes further back. Search works there too.

Chapter 07 of 14 · Routing

Needs matching

How conversations find their patient, linking one by hand, and Not a patient.

How a conversation finds its patient

Messages tries to link each new conversation to a Healthie patient on its own:

  • By a decision someone made before. If staff linked this sender to a patient earlier, their new conversations go straight to that patient: Linked automatically: staff linked this sender before. A sender marked Not a patient stays that way.
  • Email, by the exact address. One patient with that address: linked, Matched by email address. Several: Which patient?. None: No patient.
  • Texts and calls, by the phone number on the patient's file: Matched by phone number, Which patient? when the number belongs to more than one patient, or No patient when it belongs to nobody.

Automatic matching never overrides a link or a Not a patient that someone set by hand.

The Needs matching tab

Front desk and admins have a Needs matching tab next to Inbox, with a count. It lists open conversations Messages couldn't link to one patient: the No patient and Which patient? ones. Link each sender once, and their later messages go straight to the patient.

Open a conversation to see its patient panel. It says what Messages found, for example Which patient? and 2 patients use this address. Pick the one this is about.

Linking a conversation

Press Link a patient (or Pick one when Messages has candidates). Search Healthie by name or email, at least two letters. Patients Messages suggests show their name, date of birth and group; search results show name, email and group. Details opens the record without linking, so you can check the date of birth; Link links them.

The page says Patient linked. Later messages from this sender go straight to them. The link is saved for everyone, and the conversation now shows under the patient.

Not a patient

For a vendor, a newsletter or anyone who isn't a patient, press Not a patient (or This is not a patient in the search box). Their later messages skip Needs matching and show in the Inbox with a gray Not a patient chip. Linking any of their conversations to a patient later undoes it.

Changing or undoing a link

Change patient in the conversation's patient panel moves it to another patient, or marks it not a patient. The patient timeline doesn't have this button. You'll see it on the conversation right after linking it.

What can't be linked yet

  • Faxes are linked one message at a time, and that isn't built yet. Faxes stay in the Inbox as their own rows and don't appear in Needs matching.
  • Shared contacts. When one address or number reaches more than one patient (a parent writing about two children, a pharmacy), Messages undoes any link made with it and marks the conversation Shared contact. These can't be linked to one patient for now. The page says coming soon.
  • A conversation with more than five people on it can't be linked to one patient.

Work these from the Inbox. Shared-contact conversations can be answered as usual; faxes are answered in Spruce.

Chapter 08 of 14 · Routing

Handled by and hand-offs

Handing a patient to Billing or a provider, hand-backs, and the Slack alert.

Who handles a patient

Every patient has one owner: Front desk (the default), Billing as a team, or one person by name. Front desk and admins see the Handled by band under the patient card, with Front desk sees every patient. Billing and providers see the ones handed to them.

When people are tagged on the patient, the band also says Tagged: and their names, newest first. Hover over a name to see who tagged them and when. A name leaves the line when that person presses Clear. Being tagged doesn't make someone the owner: Handled by stays as it is.

The Handled by menu offers Front desk, Billing, staff who see every patient, and providers who are set up in Messages. Billing staff aren't offered by name, because Billing works as a team: hand to Billing instead.

Handing a patient off

Choose someone other than Front desk. A box opens, Hand to and their name, with room for a note: They see it with the patient, even if they cannot see the email. Press Hand off.

What happens next:

  • the note shows at the top of the patient's timeline and as a Handoff card;
  • Billing or the provider sees the patient on their list, waiting for them, until they mark it done or hand it back;
  • a provider linked for alerts gets a Slack message (see below);
  • front desk still sees the patient too.

Handing a patient to a staff member by name (someone who sees every patient anyway) doesn't put it on a separate list. Their initials show on the row and the patient falls under their Mine.

Use the note for what they need to do. Don't put more patient detail in it than the job needs. Choosing Front desk takes the patient back at once, with no note.

Hand-backs

Billing and providers send a patient back with Hand back, and the note is required. The patient returns to front desk's list as waiting, with a violet banner: Handed back to front desk by the person, with waiting for staff and their note.

That wait clears when front desk:

  • replies from Messages to someone who wrote in, or sends a text from Messages;
  • marks the patient done;
  • chooses who handles the patient.

A reply sent straight from Gmail, a forward or an internal note doesn't clear it. Mark the patient done when you've dealt with it.

The Slack alert

When front desk or an admin hands a patient to a provider by name, the provider gets a Slack direct message like this:

Synthetic Front Desk handed you a patient in Messages, with a note for you. (a link that opens the patient in Messages)

It says who handed the patient over and whether there's a note, and links to the patient. It never includes the patient's name, the note or anything from their messages. Opening the link asks them to sign in and checks they can see the patient.

There's no alert when:

  • the patient is handed to Billing or Front desk;
  • you hand a patient to yourself;
  • the patient was already waiting on their list and you added no note;
  • the person can't open Messages yet, or an admin hasn't linked their login to them and added their Slack ID (see Setting up Slack alerts and calls).

If a provider marked the patient done and you hand the patient to them again, they're alerted again.

Chapter 09 of 14 · Routing

Save to chart

Putting an attachment in the patient's Healthie documents, staff only.

Saving a file to the chart

Staff can put an attachment straight into the patient's Documents in Healthie. Next to each file in a patient's timeline (email attachments, Spruce files and voicemail recordings) is a small document icon, Save to chart. Providers don't have it.

Faxes can't be saved from Messages yet, because they can't be linked to a patient. Download the fax and add it in Healthie.

The box says Save the file to the patient's documents in Healthie. Staff only: the patient will not see it. Press Save to chart.

  • The file lands in the patient's Documents, staff only, named after the file, with Saved from Messages by your name.
  • The limit is 10 MB a file. A bigger one says This file is too large to save from here. Add it in Healthie instead.
  • The same file is only ever saved once to the same patient: Already in the patient's chart.
  • If the conversation stopped being this patient's while you had it open, the save is refused. Reload and try again.

When a save isn't confirmed

Healthie sometimes takes too long to answer. Then the page says We couldn’t confirm it was saved. Look in the patient’s documents in Healthie before saving again. Messages never saves it again on its own.

Under the timeline, a reminder lists the file: We couldn’t confirm the file was saved to this patient’s chart. The patient stays in front desk's Inbox with a Chart save to check chip until someone checks.

  1. Open the patient's Documents in Healthie.
  2. If the file is there, press I’ve checked, dismiss.
  3. If it isn't, press Save to chart on the file again. The box now asks you to check first; press It’s not there, save again.

The reminder also appears when a file was saved but its conversation moved to another patient during the save. Check in Healthie that it belongs on this chart.

Chapter 10 of 14 · Billing and providers

If you're in Billing or a provider

Your list, handing a patient back, and what you can and can't do.

Your list

If you're in Billing or a provider, your list holds only the patients front desk handed to you. A banner says so at the top:

  • Billing: You see only patients handed to Billing, and patients you're tagged on.
  • Providers: You see only patients handed to you, and patients you're tagged on, and, without email access, Email stays with front desk and billing.

You don't have Needs matching or the Handled by menu; front desk does the matching and routing. You never see conversations that aren't linked to a patient.

Providers see only Messages and their own Settings (Account and Appearance) in the sidebar, and the dashboard opens straight on Messages. There's no patient search box at the top for providers.

A patient stays on your list while there's something there for you: a conversation you can see, a hand-off note, or a hand-off still waiting for you.

Working a patient

Open the patient. A violet banner shows who handed them over and their note, with waiting for you.

You can:

  • read the conversations you have access to;
  • reply by text, and by email if you have email access (Billing always does);
  • write internal notes for the team;
  • open and download attachments;
  • send a new email, with email access;
  • call the patient from your own phone with Call (see Calling a patient), once an admin has added your phone.

Providers don't have Details (the full patient record from Healthie) or Save to chart. Open chart is there for everyone.

Finishing: Done or Hand back

When you've dealt with it, you have two choices.

  • Done closes the conversations you can see. The patient stays yours and comes back on your list when something new arrives.
  • Hand back returns the patient to front desk. Write what front desk needs to do; the note is required. The conversations you can see are marked done in the same step, and front desk sees the patient as waiting, with your note on top.

The page says Handed back to front desk, and the patient leaves your list.

When you're tagged

Front desk or an admin can tag you in an internal note to ask you to look at a patient (see Tagging a teammate). That patient then shows on your list with a Tagged chip, even if it isn't handed to you. Hover over the chip to see who tagged you and when. The Tagged filter lists the patients you're tagged on; it shows once someone has tagged you.

Open the patient. A blue banner stays at the top of the patient's page, under their name, even as you scroll. It says who tagged you and when, with their note and Clear. A long note shows two lines; Show all opens the rest.

When you're there only because of the tag, you can read the conversations you have access to, reply, write notes and call. Done, Hand back, Send and mark done, Forward, new emails and Save to chart aren't offered: whoever handles the patient does those. Without email access you see the note, but not the email.

When you've done what was asked, press Clear. The page says Tag cleared, and a patient you had only because of the tag leaves your list. A patient that's also handed to you stays. If someone tagged you again since you opened the patient, Clear asks you to read the new note first.

Slack alerts (providers)

If an admin has linked your dashboard login to you on the Users page, and your entry on the People page has your Slack ID, you get a Slack message when front desk hands you a patient. Billing gets no Slack alert, because patients go to Billing as a team. It says who handed it over and links to the patient. It never names the patient or repeats the note, so open the link to see what's needed.

You get the same kind of Slack message when someone tags you: who tagged you, and the link.

Chapter 11 of 14 · For admins

Settings › Inboxes

Connecting Gmail mailboxes and choosing which Spruce lines show in Messages.

The Inboxes page

Settings › Inboxes lists the Gmail mailboxes and Spruce lines that feed Messages. Only admins can change them; everyone else sees Only admins can connect mailboxes or change Spruce lines.

Gmail mailboxes

Each mailbox shows a badge:

  • Connected, with who connected it, when it last synced, and whether new mail shows up within seconds or within a minute.
  • Needs reconnect: Google access was lost, so mail is not syncing and its conversations are hidden from Messages. Connect it again below.
  • Disconnected, with the date and Its conversations are hidden from Messages.

While a mailbox is Needs reconnect or Disconnected, all of its conversations disappear from Messages: rows, patient timelines, counts and the From choices for new email. They come back when it's reconnected. Messages says so at the top for a mailbox that needs reconnecting: A mailbox needs reconnecting in Settings › Inboxes. Its email is hidden here until then.

Connecting a mailbox

  1. Type the mailbox address in Mailbox. It must be a @threeriversmentalhealth.com address.
  2. Press Connect.
  3. Google asks you to sign in. Sign in as this mailbox itself, not your own account, and click Allow. Leave the Gmail box checked.
  4. You come back to the page with the mailbox Connected.

If you sign in as a different account, nothing is saved: Signed in to Google as a different account than the mailbox. Start again and sign in as the mailbox.

The first sync brings in the last 14 days of mail, at most 300 messages, as history. History never reopens anything already marked done. The conversations it brings in show as open and unread, and one whose last message from outside was never answered shows as Waiting until someone replies or marks it done. Expect some catching up after connecting a mailbox.

Disconnecting

Disconnect asks first. Messages stops reading and sending from that mailbox, and Google removes its access. Nothing in the mailbox itself changes. Connecting again needs a new sign-in as the mailbox.

Spruce lines

Texts, calls, voicemails and faxes on the lines turned on here show in Messages. Turning a line off hides its conversations there, patient timelines included; turning it back on brings them back, with its last 3 days. Spruce stays as it is. Each line has a switch.

  • Turning a line on: its conversations start showing in Messages, and the last 3 days come in once, as history, shortly after. As with a new mailbox, these show as open and unread, and unanswered ones as Waiting.
  • Turning a line off: its conversations disappear from Messages, patient timelines included. Nothing changes in Spruce. Turn it back on and its last 3 days come in again.

The footer says how quickly new messages arrive and when Messages last checked Spruce.

Calls go out from

Calls go out from picks the line patients see when someone presses Call in Messages. Only phone lines that are on are listed. No calls from Messages stops calls: pressing Call then says calls aren't set up. If the chosen line is switched off above, calls stop until you choose another line or turn it back on.

Chapter 12 of 14 · For admins

Settings › Messages access

The staff switch, each person's team and extras, what the extras really do, and who each login is.

The Messages access page

Settings › Messages access decides who sees what. Roles (admin, staff, provider) come from each person's dashboard account and aren't changed here. Here you choose each person's team and anything extra they cover. Only admins can change it.

Staff can use Messages

The switch at the top, Staff can use Messages, opens Messages to everyone who is set up. Admins always can. Turn it on once the practice mailbox is connected and people are set up. Turning it off hides Messages from staff right away. It covers providers too, even though it says staff.

While it's off, the page shows Messages is open only to admins until staff access is turned on above. You can set people up first. Each row still says what that person will see once it's on, so you can check a setup before turning it on.

Setting someone up

The list shows every enabled dashboard user with their role badge (Admin, Staff, Provider or No role) and a sentence saying what they see. Not set up yet means they have no Messages setup. Admin and No role rows can't be edited.

For staff:

  • Team: Front desk or Billing.
  • Also sees: Front desk inbox, for Billing staff only. Front desk staff already see every patient and their email, so they're offered no extras.

For providers:

  • Also sees: Billing and Email. Providers have no team and can't cover the front desk inbox; someone who covers the front desk needs a staff account.

Press Set up for someone new (staff start on Front desk), or Save after a change. The change reaches their open dashboard within a minute.

What each extra does

  • Front desk inbox makes a Billing staff member work as front desk: every patient, Needs matching and Handled by, and no Hand back.
  • Billing, for a provider, adds the patients handed to Billing.
  • Email, for a provider, shows email. Without it, a provider sees only texts, calls, voicemails and notes.

The page only offers an extra where it changes something.

Who each login is

Under each person, a line says who their login is on the People page and whether Slack messages and Call work for them, for example Linked to a name, Slack messages: on. Call: off, no mobile on People. Nothing here can be changed: logins are linked to people on the Users page, and each person's Slack ID and mobile are on People (see Setting up Slack alerts and calls).

Not linked: no Slack messages or Call. Link them on Users. means the login isn't linked to anyone, so that person gets no Slack messages from Messages and can't use Call, and Messages shows the login's own name.

Your own row has a You badge, so you can tell which login you're signed in with.

If someone else changed it

If the same person was saved somewhere else while you were editing (by another admin, or by you in another tab), the page says their access was changed somewhere else while you were editing, shows what it now reads, and offers Start over from theirs. Your own save never counts as a change made elsewhere.

Chapter 13 of 14 · For admins

Setting up Slack alerts and calls

Slack IDs and mobiles on People, and linking each dashboard login to its person on Users.

What Slack alerts and calls need

When front desk or an admin hands a patient to someone in Messages, or tags them in a note, that person gets a Slack direct message with a link to the patient (see Handled by and hand-offs). It goes through the same Slack messages providers already get for appointments and unsigned notes. Call in Messages rings the caller's own mobile.

Both work the same way: Messages follows the person's dashboard login to who they are in Healthie, on the People page. That person's entry holds their Slack ID and their mobile. It works for providers and staff alike.

Adding someone's Slack ID and mobile

  1. Open People in the sidebar. Providers and Staff at the top narrow the list.
  2. Press the pencil next to the person.
  3. Fill in Slack User ID and Mobile. The same mobile gets credential reminder texts and is the phone they dial from when they press Call. Turn Active off for someone who has left: they get no Slack messages from Messages and can't use Call.
  4. Press Save.

Each person needs their own Slack ID and their own mobile. If someone else already has the one you typed, the dialog says is already on that person and Save stays off.

Only admins see full mobile numbers. Everyone else sees the last four digits.

Linking a login to a person

  1. Open Users in the sidebar (under Settings).
  2. Choose Edit user from the menu at the end of the login's row. When you invite someone new, the same field is in Invite user.
  3. Under This login is, pick the person. If someone in Healthie has the same email as the login, a link under the field offers them, ending the same email in Healthie.
  4. Press Save changes.

The Person column on Users and the Dashboard Login column on People show the link. Messages shows that person's name for the login from then on. A login can be linked to one person, and a person to one login. Picking a different person for a login moves the link. A person already linked to another login isn't offered until that login is unlinked, disabled or deleted. If someone has left Healthie, the Person column says no longer in Healthie; choose Not linked to anyone in Edit user to clear it.

Linking a login doesn't change its role. A provider's login shows its role as Provider, and it can't be changed on this page.

Not linked to anyone is right for logins that aren't anyone in Healthie, such as a test login. They get no Slack messages and can't use Call.

Checking it worked

Open Settings › Messages access. Each person's line says who their login is linked to, and whether Slack messages and Call are on. If one is off, the line says why: no Slack ID or mobile on People, or someone else has the same one.

When an alert doesn't arrive

  • The person can't use Messages yet. Check Staff can use Messages and their setup in Settings › Messages access.
  • Their login isn't linked to them on Users, or their entry on People has no Slack ID.
  • Someone else on People has the same Slack ID.
  • They're marked inactive on People.
  • They already had the patient waiting on their list, and the hand-off had no note.

Alerts never hold up the hand-off: if Slack is slow or down, the patient is still handed over. A new link or Slack ID can take a few minutes to start working.

Chapter 14 of 14 · Help

When something looks wrong

Missing conversations, unconfirmed sends, lost drafts, and who to ask.

Something seems to be missing

  • A whole mailbox's email is gone. The top of Messages says A mailbox needs reconnecting in Settings › Inboxes. Its email is hidden here until then. An admin reconnects it there.
  • Texts from one line are gone. That Spruce line may have been switched off in Settings › Inboxes.
  • I can't find a patient by name. Search matches the name as Healthie spells it. Try part of the name, or their email, or search by the email's subject or sender. A patient with no conversations in Messages has no row to find.
  • A conversation isn't under the patient. It may be in Needs matching, or marked Shared contact, or be a fax. See Needs matching.
  • I only see some patients. Billing and providers see only patients handed to them. See Who sees what.
  • Messages isn't in my sidebar, or says it's not open to me. Ask an admin to check Settings › Messages access.

Call doesn't connect

  • The box says my phone or calls aren't set up. Ask an admin: your phone goes in Settings › Messages access, and the line calls go out from in Settings › Inboxes.
  • I dialed and nothing happened. Dial from the phone ending in the digits the box shows, and dial straight away. Close the box, press Call again, and dial the new number.
  • Healthie has no number for the patient. Add it in Healthie, then try again.

A send says Not confirmed

Wait a few minutes, then look before sending again: at the timeline, the mailbox's Sent folder in Gmail, or the conversation in Spruce. Messages never retries on its own, so nothing goes out twice unless you send it twice. See Replying and notes.

My draft disappeared

Drafts live only on the page. Messages asks before you leave a draft behind, and your browser warns before a reload or closing the tab. An idle sign-out or a change to your access still loses it without asking, so don't leave a long reply unsent when you step away.

Done left something open

Done never closes a conversation that changed after you opened the patient. Read what's new, then press Done again. A conversation that couldn't be loaded stays open until it loads.

The page says it's reconnecting

Reconnecting. This patient is hidden until it refreshes. means the dashboard couldn't confirm your access for a few minutes, usually a network blip. It comes back on its own. Your draft is kept.

Who to ask

For access, mailboxes, Spruce lines or anything that looks broken, ask your dashboard admin. Don't send patient details over Slack or email to explain a problem; say which row or patient ID, and what you expected.
